colorRoles: Use neutral off-brand colors for the broken assistant UI.
Reserve stronger contrast for payment failure and blocked states.
Use Lucius purple only as a restrained closing-tag quality cue.
typeRoles: Use sans-serif only in the negative example UI.
Use one strong headline layer with restrained support labels.
Keep any Lucius closing tag secondary.
radiusRules: Use soft, consistent rounded corners across chat and payment surfaces.
Do not mix incompatible corner languages.
backgroundRules: Use a warm neutral background with quiet depth.
Keep the background restrained so the proof element remains dominant.
graphicLanguage: Use clean SaaS UI surfaces and minimal chrome.
Avoid decorative clutter or joke framing.
motionTone: Motion should feel quietly confident and readable.
The final proof state should end in a dead-stop hold.
prohibitedPatterns: No flashy AI magic or glitch spectacle.
No competing animated elements on the same screen.

colorRoles: Use neutral slate and ivory surfaces for the broken assistant UI.
Use red-toned contrast for payment failure states.
Use Lucius purple only in the restrained closing tag.
typeRoles: Keep body copy short and quiet.
radiusRules: Use one coherent rounded-card system across all surfaces.
spacingRules: Keep generous whitespace between headline, chat card, and payment proof surface.
backgroundRules: Use a soft warm gradient with a subtle grid texture.
motionRules: Use one dominant motion per screen.
Allow only supporting transitions around the main motion.
End the final proof screen in a dead-stop hold.

screens.goal: Make the money-related failure obvious at first glance.
layout: Use a left-weighted complaint card with minimal surrounding UI chrome.
background: Use a warm neutral canvas with a subtle grid.
screens.primaryMotion: Complaint card slides in and settles.

screens.goal: Show polished reassurance without useful action.
screens.uiSurface: assistant reply bubble in the same chat
layout: Keep the complaint readable but secondary while one reply bubble becomes focal.
background: Keep the same chat environment from screen 01.
screens.primaryMotion: Assistant comfort bubble expands softly into view.
proofElement: The reply contains no real fix or operational next step.

screens.goal: Escalate frustration with a false solved signal.
screens.uiSurface: quick user pushback plus reply state
layout: Use a compact exchange with one dominant solved badge and reply card.
background: Use the same chat environment with a slightly tighter crop.
screens.primaryMotion: The false resolved state lands abruptly.
proofElement: Resolved appears before any real product change.

screens.goal: Prove the product is still blocked after the fake resolution.
layout: Use one large payment panel that dominates the frame.
background: Use a warm neutral backdrop and remove chat from focus.
screens.primaryMotion: Hard cut into the payment panel followed by a dead-stop hold.

implementationNotes: Keep the negative assistant visually competent but not Lucius-branded.
Reserve the Lucius close for the final edge of the piece only.
The payment panel must dominate the final proof screen and remain readable in silence.
acceptanceChecks: Every screen has one primary motion only.
The final proof screen is undeniable at first glance.
Brand constraints stay visible in color, type, radius, background, and motion tone.
